chunks: As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from al-Naḍr ibn Suwayd, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḥumayd, from Abī Baṣīr, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
"Stoning is the greater hadd of Allah, and flogging is the lesser hadd of Allah. So when the muḥṣan man commits zina, he is stoned and not flogged."

So this does not contradict the reports we mentioned earlier regarding the obligation of combining stoning and flogging, because it can bear two possibilities. One of them is that it was issued by way of taqiyyah, because none of the ʿāmmah agree with us on this ruling, and in matters of this kind taqiyyah is permissible. The second possibility is that what is meant by it is one who is not an old man, but rather is young, because the one upon whom both stoning and flogging become obligatory is when he is an old muḥṣan. He عليه السلام clarified that in the narration of ʿAbdullāh ibn Ṭalḥah, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj, al-Ḥalabī, Zurārah, and ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, which we mentioned earlier. Nor does what Muḥammad ibn Qays narrated in the report cited earlier from his statement, "The old man and the old woman are to be flogged one hundred [lashes]," contradict this, even though he did not mention stoning, because it is not impossible that he did not mention stoning since there is no disagreement concerning its obligation upon the muḥṣan, and he mentioned flogging, which is specifically added as obligatory upon him together with stoning, and so he limited himself to that because the addressee knew of the obligation of combining the two. Moreover, it is also possible that the narration is restricted to the case where they are not muḥṣanayn. Do you not see that he then said after that: and he ruled concerning the two muḥṣanayn that they are to be stoned, even though the obligation of stoning for the two muḥṣanayn is agreed upon, whether one is old or young.

key_terms.التَّقِيَّةِ: dissimulation or precautionary concealment in cases of risk
key_terms.الشَّيْخُ: an old man, used here in determining a specific legal application
key_terms.الْعَامَّةِ: the Sunni majority or general non-Imami community in this context
key_terms.الْمُحْصَنَيْنِ: the two legally protected married offenders
key_terms.الْمُحْصَنُ: a legally protected married person subject to the ruling of iḥṣān

ai.seo_question: How do Shia hadith reconcile reports about stoning and flogging for a muḥṣan adulterer?
ai.summary: This passage discusses the legal ruling concerning the hadd for zina in the case of a muḥṣan man and reconciles apparently differing reports on whether stoning alone or both stoning and flogging are to be applied. It explains that some narrations may have been issued under taqiyyah or may refer specifically to younger offenders, while other reports establish the combined ruling for an elderly muḥṣan offender.
